correctness.rationale: For a \(P\)-point, every continuous approximate norming function is locally equal to one near p; the countable intersection property gives a common neighborhood, and Urysohn's lemma gives a common positive minorant g with g(p)=1 and norm exactly one. If p is not a \(P\)-point, closed complements F_n of a witnessing sequence of neighborhoods define a lattice norm between the supremum norm and twice that norm. Test functions supported in finite intersections show the evaluation dual norm is one, while continuity forces every candidate with |f(p)|=1 to incur a strictly positive restriction penalty. The proof covers both signs and needs no sequential convergence assumption.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete pointwise criterion for when evaluation norm-attainment is invariant under all equivalent lattice renormings. It also supplies an explicit equivalent norm for every failure of the topological condition, including nonsequential cases left outside the earlier sequence-based construction. This resolves a natural boundary left by the robust ordinal endpoint example and the general existence theorem.
